articles.title: Final Fantasy’s Yoshinori Kitase Teases What’s Next for Square Enix, Says Company Will Prioritize New Games Over Remakes
articles.summary: Final Fantasy producer Yoshinori Kitase reveals Square Enix will prioritize new games over remakes, discussing future film adaptations and what he wants to make next.
body: Final Fantasy VII Revelation is still months away, but a prominent voice in the Final Fantasy universe is already teasing what’s next for publisher Square Enix after the game releases next year.

I spoke exclusively with Yoshinori Kitase, who serves as producer of the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy, director of the original Final Fantasy VII (along with Final Fantasy VI, VIII, X, and Chrono Trigger), and brand manager of the Final Fantasy franchise at Square Enix, at the Lucca Comics & Games Festival 2026.

We spoke at length about Kitase’s decades-long involvement in the Final Fantasy franchise, and why he’s ready to turn the page. During the conversation, Kitase shared plans about what’s next for Square Enix, if he’s still interested in film adaptations, and which Final Fantasy game fans inside and outside the company want to remake next.

IGN: I want to of course talk about Final Fantasy, but also Square Enix in general. Square Enix is very famous for both new IP and also remakes. How do you balance that as a company? Are they both equally important to the company at this moment and also moving forward?
points: Final Fantasy producer Yoshinori Kitase reveals Square Enix will prioritize new games over remakes, discussing future film adaptations and what he wants to make next.

articles.title: God of War Laufey Delayed to May 2027
articles.summary: God of War Laufey will no longer be released in February, as Sony Santa Monica has pushed it back to May 2027. The game will now launch on May 20, 2027, with the studio stating that it needs more time to make a product that meets fans' expectations.
body: God of War Laufey had previously been slated to release on February 16, 2027. This window has become exceptionally crowded, especially after some games like Fable pivoted from a fall 2026 release to early 2027 to avoid the blast zone of GTA 6. This will not only give God of War some space to breathe, but potentially allow other games to stretch their wings that may not be as high on the priority list for gamers compared to a new first-party PlayStation game.

God of War Laufey has been met with no shortage of skepticism and criticism from some gamers, partially due to the fact that Kratos has been sidelined as the main character. As a result, it will be important for Santa Monica Studio to be on their A-game and deliver something exceptional. If there's anything that falls short of expectations, the internet will ruthlessly pick it apart, regardless of it's actually fair to do so.
points: God of War Laufey will no longer be released in February, as Sony Santa Monica has pushed it back to May 2027.

articles.title: God Of War Laufey Delayed
articles.summary: Santa Monica Studios has delayed God of War Laufey. The new God of War game for PS5 is no longer set for release in February 2027, and has shifted to May 2027. The game will now launch on May 20, 2027, which is a delay of about three months from its original February 16, 2027 release date.
body: "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," the developer said. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."
God of War Laufey stars Deborah Ann Woll as Faye. Starring alongside Woll is The Boys actor Jack Quaid, who plays a gelatinous cube named Phranque.

Compared to Kratos and his skillful application of brute force to help solve problems, Faye is far more graceful and nimble. Like the previous games, God of War Laufey is a third-person action experience built around chaining together various skills and weapons to dish out tremendous amounts of damage.
You can see the game in action in the gameplay trailer below.

articles.summary: Dr. Doom is teaming up with a particularly powerful ally: Colonel Sanders. KFC announced its official Avengers: Doomsday campaign with a commercial showing Dr. Doom looking out on the Fallout-esque ruins of New York.
body: "KFC has come to an agreement with Dr. Doom," says the overlay. "All it took was a meal worthy of his name."
Fans will get the chance to try this meal for themselves when the official Dr. Doom menu launches across select KFC locations on November 9.

Every "Doomified" purchase comes in limited-edition packaging inspired by Dr. Doom's green and black look, and also comes with one of five Colonel Sanders Cosplay Collection figurines, while supplies last.

The Doom-approved menu is powered by three new flavors: a Smoky Green Mayo, a sweet and caramelized Doom Cola sauce, and a smoky charred lime and chili seasoning KFC is calling Doom Dust. The Dr. Doom Menu adds various combinations of these new flavors to existing KFC classics, like Dripped Wings, Loaded Fries, and the classic Chicken Bucket.

articles.title: Nexus Mods Won’t Ban AI Mods, But It Won’t Let Them Hide Either
articles.summary: Nexus Mods owner Victor "Foledinho" Folmann has outlined plans to make AI disclosures mandatory for PC mods uploaded to the site. While content built with AI tools won't be banned--despite it being a contentious subject in the modding community--Folmann did reveal that Nexus Mods will ultimately…
body: "We already have tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods, but we recognize that there’s a lot more we can do to make that information more accessible and clear for you all," Folmann wrote. "As of today, we're making AI disclosure mandatory when uploading a new mod, meaning mod authors will need to declare whether AI has been used in their work. All existing mods will have one of two popups: a persistent one when editing a mod in the upload form, and a dismissible one on the 'My Mods' page."

At the same time, Nexus Mods users will be able to filter out AI-produced mods entirely from their search results, similar to what Itch.io does as part of its efforts to combat AI spam uploads. As for why Nexus Mods will allow AI content to remain on the site, Folmann added that an outright ban would likely lead modders to simply not declare their use of AI tools in their mod-creation-efforts. By allowing and moderating it, the site can motivate users to be more transparent.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Is Still 2+ Years Away From Release – Report
articles.summary: Bethesda just recently lifted the lid on the next Elder Scrolls game, revealing its title to be "Sentinel" and telling fans it will be "some time" before more is shared. But just when could Sentinel be released?
body: "TESVI: Sentinel is more than two years away," he wrote on Reddit.

The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced more than eight years ago, and until this week, Bethesda hadn't said much at all in an official capacity about the game. The latest information wasn't much to go on, either, as Bethesda only confirmed the game's title and published a title card video featuring a scroll emerging from the sand. The video also hinted that Hammerfell being the game's location.

Game director Todd Howard has questioned whether it was the right call to announce The Elder Scrolls 6 so early. “I have asked myself that a lot,” he said. “I don’t know. I probably would’ve announced it more casually.”
He later said announcing The Elder Scrolls 6 in the way that Bethesda did was “not my preference,” but it happened anyway.

articles.title: PS Plus Makes James Bond’s New Game Free for Just One Hour
articles.summary: 007 First Light starts with a bang. James Bond’s latest mission begins with a cold-open action sequence that segues into one of the best video game tutorials in recent memory. PlayStation Plus members can now try that impressive introduction for free.
body: Video game tutorials are famously Not Very Good. Many are dull introductions that over-explain every gameplay system in exhaustive detail instead of letting players put things together for themselves. Even in cinematic, story-focused games, pop-up menus clog the screen, making it impossible to get lost in the world.

A main difference with First Light ’s tutorial is that it happens in-universe. You come to learn how the game works alongside Bond’s in-universe training, as the neophyte spy learns the tools of the trade in a playable training montage that jump-cuts between different set pieces. There are car races, fistfights, and mock infiltration missions where Bond tries to earn his place in a program that virtually no one thinks he belongs in. The sequence is stylish and provides a narrative buy-in that most game tutorials don’t even attempt.

At least based on 007 First Light' s sales, it seems quite possible the game will get a sequel. After launching in May, 007 First Light had already sold an impressive 4 million copies by August, making it one of the best-selling games of 2026 so far.

articles.title: Is The Gears Of War Movie Actually Going To Happen? Director Weighs In
articles.summary: A Gears of War movie is in development at Netflix, but is it ever going to happen? That remains to be seen, but director David Leitch of John Wick fame recently said the movie will "hopefully" come to fruition "soon." Speaking to ScreenRant, Leitch said, "I think everybody's excited about the…
body: He added: "I wish I could tell you more, because there's some much cool stuff going on."

Netflix recently underwent a big shift in management, with film chief Dan Lin exiting the company alongside longtime chief content officer Bela Bajaria. Former Former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice is now the new chief content officer. He was only just recently installed in the post, so it remains to be seen what changes Rice could make. There is, however, precedent for new management making big changes, as Netflix's BioShock movie was scaled back under the leadership of Lin.
The latest script for the Gears of War movie as of 2025 was written by Jon Spaihts, who previously wrote Prometheus, Doctor Strange, and Passengers, along with Dune 1 and 2.

Gears of War fans have been waiting decades for their promised Gears of War movie. All the way back in 2007, a year after the first Gears of War game came out, New Line Cinema purchased the rights to make a movie based on the game. Nothing ever came of that. Then in 2016, the Gears of War movie rights changed hands and went to Universal. Nothing came of that, either.

articles.title: GTA 6 Sells Nearly 8 Million Copies Before It Even Launches, Report Says
articles.summary: The anticipation surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 is reaching a fever pitch as Rockstar Games' long-awaited open-world adventure gets closer to its launch. Between fans dissecting every trailer, an alligator Xbox sweepstakes capitalizing on the hype, and players preparing their hard drives for the…
body: Now, new estimates suggest that the excitement is already translating into some seriously impressive sales figures. According to data from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has reportedly sold approximately 7.71 million copies ahead of its Nov. 19 release. That's translated to an estimated $751 million in revenue, despite not being available to play yet.

Sensor Tower's figures suggest that PlayStation accounts for 74% of those sales, with Xbox making up the remaining 26%. While Rockstar has yet to officially confirm its preorder numbers, the estimates offer an interesting glimpse into just how enormous the demand for GTA 6 has become.
To put those numbers into perspective, GTA 6 is already comfortably in the conversation among 2026's best-selling games, despite still being more than two weeks away from launch.

The latest year-to-date sales rankings from Circana offer a useful snapshot of the competition. Its current top ten includes major releases such as NBA 2K27, Resident Evil: Requiem, 007 First Light, MLB: The Show 26, Crimson Desert, and Call of Duty: Black Ops II.

articles.title: 5 Elder Scrolls 6 Fan Theories That Should Actually Happen In Sentinel
articles.summary: For its 40th anniversary, legendary developer Bethesda gave its fans the best possible gift: another The Elder Scrolls 6 tease. Yeah. But wait, this time, we got a title! One that the community had already guessed years ago. But beggars can’t be choosers.
body: Meanwhile, fans have new material to feed their theories about The Elder Scrolls 6: a title, Sentinel, and a juicy quote from a Moth Priest. Since the game was announced in 2018, theories have proliferated (there’s nothing else we can do, after all!). Some have been proven true, some will quite likely be proven true, and some are just absurd, but we still would like to see them come to fruition.

Let’s start with an easy one. Speculation that Hammerfell will be the setting of the next game in the series began with the first teaser shown in 2018. The geography and environmental features pointed to the Redguards' homeland, and the Nov. 3 reveal confirmed it. Sentinel is a major city in Hammerfell, also present in The Elder Scrolls Online, and the quote shared with the teaser is attributed to a Moth Priest serving High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

body: Developer Sony Santa Monica announced it's pushing back the upcoming action epic via a brief social media post. While the studio stopped short of giving a reason for the delay, it did say it's using the extra time to polish Faye's solo adventure.

"Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we've been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye's journey through the Everywhen. We don't take for granted the trust placed in the studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication of our fans," the studio wrote.

"With this in mind, we've made the decision to delay God of War Laufey's release to May 20th, 2027," the statement continued. "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential. On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

articles.title: Where to use the blackmarket weapons locker key in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4
articles.summary: The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ blackmarket weapons locker key is one of many keys in the extraction mode, and it's used to open, as you may have guessed from its name, a locker that can contain rare weapons and loot.
body: Here's a complete guide on where you need to go to use the blackmarket weapons locker key in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4.

There are two locations where you can use the blackmarket weapons locker key in DMZ, and each location has two lockers. So if you have multiple keys, you can grab the goodies from up to four locked containers in one deployment. The image above shows where both blackmarket weapons lockers can be found, at both Hanrin Village and Deadtown, along with the building you're looking for.

When you've found the correct building, indicated by the wrought iron gates on the front and the red advert above it for an MP3 player, head inside and look for the stairs down to the basement. Go through another door and you'll discover the two lockers in a room with a few other lootable containers, pictured above.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel fans ponder split timelines, alternative histories, and more as story speculation runs wild following latest teaser
articles.summary: Following the release of yesterday's brief new The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel teaser trailer, story speculation is running rampant across communities dedicated to the fantasy series, with fans theorising everything from alternative histories to split timelines.
body: Yesterday's teaser - which arrived as part of Bethesda's 40th anniversary celebrations and comes amid devastating cuts across Xbox's first-party studios - was minimal. It opened with a shot of desert sand, before revealing the subtitle 'Sentinel' and ending with a quote from an unknown character. It's not much to go on, but is proving just enough to encourage discussion around what may be in store for Bethesda's next RPG.

And a good place to start is that quote. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes," it reads. "A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate." All this is attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell,, but some fans think the accompanying date - 4E 206 - might be just as significant.

"[Sentinel] likely takes place five or more years after the start of Skyrim," hypothesised Reddit user 04nc1n9. "Hammerfell is a monarchy, it hasn't changed to any other political system after their imperial secession. The monarchy of Hammerfell has a Moth Priest on hand, even though the Moth Priests are generally an Imperial thing. Hammerfell's monarch has access to an Elder Scroll after the Elder Scrolls scattered."

articles.title: Eight years ago the idea of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel had me captivated, but can Bethesda recapture the magic?
articles.summary: Eight years ago, I sat at my desk enthralled. Bethesda had just released the first trailer for The Elder Scrolls 6, a then mysteriously nameless, locationless sequel to one of the biggest games of all time, and I reckoned I'd just found the secrets to both.
body: Admittedly, I'm maybe a little more horrified at my level of Elder Scrolls obsession than I am chuffed at any apparent clairvoyance. Ultimately it was a bit of a punt, launched off the back of a day's worth of fanatical hyperfocus and exactly the right amount of the old Gamer Network office's weapons-grade filter coffee. "There's not really a lot to go on here", I wrote, sagely, "but, if we had to, we'd plant our flag in Hammerfell as the location of The Elder Scrolls 6."

Indulge me a bit and let's retread the reasoning. First, three assumptions were required in order to make any kind of guess at all: The Elder Scrolls 6 would not be set in all of Tamriel; not set outside of Tamriel; and would be set somewhere vaguely close in the timeline to the events of Morrowind, Oblivion and Skyrim - so as to make that bit of scrabbly rock and ruined castle, visible in that now infamous first teaser, at least somewhat traceable with contemporary descriptions in the lore.

videos.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Review
videos.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time reviewed by Logan Plant on Nintendo Switch 2.
body: "It’s in our nature to pass old stories down, and I think there’s meaning in the ones we choose to revisit. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is both an exceptional remake of an incredible game and a rich adventure that stands on its own. This remake proves there’s still so much value in the traditional Zelda formula: the dense, intimate world of Hyrule is stuffed with charming characters and fascinating secrets. Its intricate dungeons are satisfying to unravel, even if their somewhat streamlined design has slightly dulled the special feeling that comes from solving them. Still, the depth, quality, and attention to detail in every corner match the lofty reputation of this series. Whether you’ve played the original 100 times, once back in 1998, or never at all, I highly recommend this beautiful retelling of a legend."

videos.summary: Check out the teaser trailer for Lords of War, an upcoming movie starring Nicolas Cage, Bill Skarsgård, Laura Harrier, Sylvia Hoeks, and Greg Tarzan Davis.
body: Academy Award winner Nicolas Cage reprises his role as Yuri Orlov, the world’s most notorious arms dealer. When Yuri discovers a ruthless mercenary mastermind (Bill Skarsgård) bent on destroying his legacy is building a private army, he is thrust into a blood-soaked and bullet-riddled battle to the death. What begins as a shocking revelation ignites a fierce rivalry fueled by power, ambition, and betrayal.
Lords of War is produced by Philippe Rousselet, Fabrice Gianfermi, Andrew Niccol, and Nicolas Cage.
Lords of War, written and directed by Andrew Niccol, opens in US theaters on January 22, 2027.

videos.title: SCSKiller - The Beginning Of The End For PC #StutterStruggle?
videos.summary: Many thanks to Alienware for sponsoring this video. To learn more about Alienware’s 39-inch 5K OLED Gaming Monitor, check it out here:
body: It's been years now since Digital Foundry began its campaign against intrusive stuttering in PC games and while there has been fundamental change in PC gaming, it's still an issue in many new titles. Meanwhile, a massive back catalogue of releases may never receive official updates to resolve the issue. Enter SCSKiller - an app inspired by Alex's anti-stutter campaign, put together by DF Supporter BlueHeisenberg - that aims to take an external, brute force approach to the issue. It's not perfect, but it is capable of some astonishing results.
